text: In New York he bought fine clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> Silk underwear, and silver mounted brushes. <break time="0.8s" /> And he took rooms at the Waldorf. <break time="0.8s" /> Explaining that he was from Washington. <break time="0.8s" /> And that his parents were abroad. <break time="0.8s" /> Surrounded by flowers, soft carpets. <break time="0.8s" /> And music drifting up from the dining room. <break time="0.8s" /> He felt that this was exactly. <break time="0.8s" /> What all the struggle of his life had been about. <break time="0.8s" /> One night he went out. <break time="0.8s" /> With a wild boy from San Francisco. <break time="0.8s" /> A freshman at Yale. <break time="0.8s" /> And they stayed out until dawn. <break time="0.8s" /> But in the morning they parted singularly cool. <break time="0.8s" /> He felt no remorse. <break time="0.8s" /> For here, as he glanced down at his dress coat. <break time="0.8s" /> He was sure. <break time="0.8s" /> That it would be impossible. <break time="0.8s" /> For anyone to humiliate him. <break time="0.8s" /> On the eighth morning. <break time="0.8s" /> He found his own story in a Pittsburgh paper. <break time="0.8s" /> Which reported that his father had repaid the money. <break time="0.8s" /> And was coming to New York. <break time="0.8s" /> To bring him home. <break time="0.8s" /> The gray monotony of Cordelia Street. <break time="0.8s" /> Stretched before him. <break time="0.8s" /> In hopeless, unrelieved years. <break time="0.8s" /> Of Sunday school, yellow wallpaper, and damp dish towels. <break time="0.8s" /> And he could not bear it. <break time="0.8s" /> He left the city. <break time="0.8s" /> And wandered out into the snowy country. <break time="0.8s" /> Beside the railroad. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the red carnations in his coat. <break time="0.8s" /> Had already drooped. <break time="0.8s" /> And lost their glory in the cold. <break time="0.8s" /> It seemed to him. <break time="0.8s" /> That the flowers had had only one splendid breath. <break time="0.8s" /> For all their brave mockery at the winter. <break time="0.8s" /> And he buried one of them gently in the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> When the train came near through the falling snow. <break time="0.8s" /> Paul stepped toward it. <break time="0.8s" /> And there Cather ends his story. <break time="0.8s" /> Letting him drop back. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the immense design of things.
